messages.subject: ctmm-user@googlegroups.com
parts:
Hi ctmm team and community,

I am attempting to fit an integrated Resource Selection Function (ctmm::rsf.fit()) for a segmented individual dataset (cl_s2) using two continuous environmental predictors (elevation, dist_to_water) and one categorical land use / land cover raster (lulc_code).

Following the package documentation for categorical variables (raster::as.factor()), I attached a Raster Attribute Table (RAT) to the factor raster. However, when executing rsf.fit() with the reference argument specified, the function throws the following error: Error in reference[NAME] <- REF : replacement has length zero


Before running rsf.fit(), I verified that:

  1. All rasters are fully loaded in system RAM (raster::inMemory() evaluates to TRUE).

  2. Telemetry data and raster layers share the exact same spatial projection.

  3. Zero missing values (NAs) exist at telemetry locations.

  4. The RAT table is structured as a strict 2-column data frame (ID, lulc_code), and "Forest" is confirmed present in Column 2.

Questions

  1. Is there a specific format required for the S4 RasterLayer RAT slot so that rsf.fit() can extract the factor level names during reference indexing?


Versions of the R and packages:
R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24 ucrt)
'ctmm' version 1.3.0
‘raster’ version 3.6-32

I am uploading the document containing console for reference.  I really appreciate any suggestions or help in resolving this. Thank you for developing such a fantastic package and for ongoing support to the community.
